gloss: to have trouble with; to be a handful; to be at one's wit's end

definitions.gloss: to have trouble with; to be a handful; to be at one's wit's end
definitions.explanation: To struggle with handling someone or something difficult. Often used for children, pets, or problematic situations that resist one's efforts to manage them.

examples.japanese: {息子|むすこ}には{手|て}を{焼|や}いている。
この{問題|もんだい}には{随分|ずいぶん}{手|て}を{焼|や}いた。
examples.english: I really struggled with this problem.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}でさえ、{彼|かれ}には{手|て}を{焼|や}いている。
examples.english: Even the teacher is having trouble handling him.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいパソコンの{設定|せってい}に{手|て}を{焼|や}いた。
examples.english: I had a hard time setting up the new computer.

examples.japanese: {子犬|こいぬ}がいたずらばかりするので、{手|て}を{焼|や}いている。
examples.english: The puppy keeps getting into mischief, so it's quite a handful.

notes:
IDIOM ORIGIN:
Literally "to burn one's hand." The image is of being burned while trying to handle something hot (difficult), suggesting the difficulty and frustration of dealing with a challenging person or situation.

COMMON PATTERNS:
〜に{手|て}を{焼|や}く - to have trouble with ~, to struggle with ~

- {手|て}を{焼|や}く (present)
- {手|て}を{焼|や}いている (progressive - currently struggling)
- {手|て}を{焼|や}いた (past)
- {手|て}を{焼|や}かされる (causative-passive - to be made to struggle)

COMMON SUBJECTS:
- {子供|こども} - children
- {生徒|せいと} - students
- {部下|ぶか} - subordinates
- ペット - pets
- {問題|もんだい} - problems

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手|て}に{負|お}えない - to be unmanageable
- {持|も}て{余|あま}す - to have more than one can handle
- {頭|あたま}を{悩|なや}ます - to worry over, to rack one's brains
- {扱|あつか}いに{困|こま}る - to have trouble handling

REGISTER:
Neutral. Common in everyday conversation.
